title: Environment variables and secrets in the build process

videos.script:
On a server, an environment variable is read while the program runs. A front end has no such moment. By the time a browser opens the page, the build is over.

{{baked}} So this lesson starts by watching a variable disappear into the bundle. You set it before the build, and afterwards it is a string in a JavaScript file, like any other.

{{files}} Then the files Vite reads them from, and which one wins. And the prefix, VITE underscore, that decides what reaches the browser at all.

{{secret}} Then the uncomfortable part. Anything in the bundle is something every visitor can read. A key that must stay secret cannot live in a front end, whatever it is called. You will put one there on purpose, and find it with grep.

{{hosts}} After that, where the values come from on a host, and why a preview build and a production build get different ones.

{{leak}} And the morning after: a secret committed by mistake. What git remembers, and the one fix that works.
